text.en: Meena read that every child has a right to education. "Who gave us rights?" she asked.

Human rights are the basic rights every person has simply by being human, such as life, liberty and equality. The United Nations adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights on 10 December 1948, and we mark it as Human Rights Day.
In India the Constitution gives Fundamental Rights, including equality, freedom, protection against exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights and the right to constitutional remedies. Children also have rights to education and protection.
Rights come with duties. The National and State Human Rights Commissions look into violations, and courts protect rights.
Human rights are the basic rights every person has simply by being human, such as life, liberty and equality.
The United Nations adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights on 10 December 1948, and we mark it as Human Rights Day.

In India the Constitution gives Fundamental Rights, including equality, freedom, protection against exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights and the right to constitutional remedies.
Children also have rights to education and protection.
Rights come with duties.
The National and State Human Rights Commissions look into violations, and courts protect rights.
Human rights are universal, meaning they belong to every human being everywhere, and inalienable, meaning they cannot be unfairly stripped away because of birth, race, gender or belief.
After the horrors of World War II, nations came together in the United Nations and adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, or UDHR, on 10 December 1948.
That is why 10 December is observed worldwide every year as Human Rights Day. The UDHR contains thirty articles covering dignity, liberty, equality, education and fair trials.
Human rights fall into broad families: civil and political rights like free speech and voting, and economic, social and cultural rights like education, healthcare and fair wages.
In India, core human rights are guaranteed as Fundamental Rights in Part III of the Constitution, covering Articles 12 to 35.
Let us review the six Fundamental Rights. First, the Right to Equality forbids discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth, and abolishes untouchability.
Second, the Right to Freedom protects freedom of speech, peaceful assembly, movement, profession, and the right to life and personal liberty.
Third, the Right against Exploitation bans human trafficking, forced labour, and employing children under fourteen in hazardous factories or mines.
Fourth, the Right to Freedom of Religion lets every person practise and follow any faith—or none—peacefully. Fifth, Cultural and Educational Rights protect minority languages and scripts.

Sixth, the Right to Constitutional Remedies lets any citizen approach the Supreme Court or High Courts if their Fundamental Rights are violated. Dr B. R. Ambedkar called it the heart and soul of the Constitution.
Alongside rights, Part IV-A lists eleven Fundamental Duties—such as respecting the Constitution, protecting forests and rivers, promoting harmony, and educating children.

board.text: Rights go hand in hand with Fundamental Duties

text.en: To investigate rights violations, India set up the National Human Rights Commission, or NHRC, in 1993, and Tamil Nadu established its State Human Rights Commission in 1997.
Children have special protection under the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child: the right to survival, protection from abuse, education and participation.
Under India's Right to Education Act of 2009, free and compulsory elementary education is a guaranteed right for every child aged six to fourteen.
The POCSO Act strictly protects children from sexual offences, and the national Childline helpline 1098 offers free twenty-four-hour emergency support to any child in danger.
Women's rights are protected by laws guaranteeing equal pay for equal work, maternity benefits, inheritance rights, and protection against domestic violence and workplace harassment.
Labour rights ensure minimum wages, safe working conditions, reasonable hours, and freedom from bonded labour.

board.text: Labour rights: fair pay & safe work

text.en: Under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, elderly parents have a legal right to care and dignified living.

board.text: Senior citizens' right to care & dignity

text.en: The Right to Information Act of 2005 empowers citizens to request public records from government offices, fighting secrecy and corruption.
Remember the golden rule of rights: your freedom ends where another person's rights begin. Freedom of speech never justifies hate speech, bullying or violence.
In everyday school life, respecting human rights means standing against bullying, welcoming classmates of every background, and listening politely to different opinions.

text.en: If someone's rights are violated, remedies include approaching school authorities, Childline 1098, police, legal aid clinics, the State Human Rights Commission or the courts.

board.text: Where to seek help if rights are violated

text.en: To analyse any rights case, identify which Fundamental Right applies, whether a duty was neglected, and which legal remedy protects the victim.
Knowing our human rights—and defending the rights of others—builds a fair, peaceful and compassionate society for all.

board.text: Know your rights, respect everyone's dignity

problem.en: A twelve-year-old child is made to work ten hours a day in a fireworks workshop instead of attending school. Which Fundamental Rights and laws are violated?

text.en: Identify the Constitutional rights violated.

why.en: Employing a child under fourteen in hazardous work violates the Right against Exploitation (Article 24) and the Right to Education (Article 21A).

text.en: Identify the protective laws and helpline.

why.en: This breaks the Child Labour Prohibition Act and the RTE Act (2009); Childline 1098 can be called immediately for rescue.

text.en: State the rightful outcome.

why.en: The child must be rescued from hazardous labour and enrolled in free, compulsory schooling.

prompt.en: A friend says Human rights were declared by India in 1948. How will you reply?

points.en: Fundamental Rights are in the Constitution.
